title: James Davolos on The Noble Update Podcast: Rates Aren’t Coming to Save You (September 12, 2026)
gist: A landing page for a Noble Update Podcast episode summarizes Horizon Kinetics' James Davolos arguing that the end of the zero-interest-rate era favors a structural rotation out of high-multiple, cheap-capital-dependent growth equities and into capital-light real assets, scarce commodity royalties, and infrastructure oligopolies with inflation-indexed cash flows.

insights.claim: The end of the zero-interest-rate era structurally disadvantages high-multiple growth equities that depended on cheap capital to justify their valuations.
insights.speaker: James Davolos
insights.so_what: Investors should stress-test long-duration growth holdings for valuation support that assumed persistently cheap capital, since that regime is presented as over.
insights.quote: the end of the zero-interest-rate era and what it means for investors

insights.claim: Davolos favors rotating out of cheap-capital-dependent growth stocks into capital-light real assets, scarce commodity royalties, and infrastructure oligopolies.
insights.speaker: James Davolos
insights.so_what: Watch for royalty and infrastructure names with pricing power and low reinvestment needs as a hedge against a higher-for-longer rate regime.
insights.quote: a structural shift away from high-multiple growth equities dependent on cheap capital and toward capital-light real assets, scarce commodity royalties, and infrastructure oligopolies capable of generating inflation-indexed cash flows

insights.claim: The preferred real-asset holdings generate inflation-indexed cash flows, positioning them as a hedge against a durable higher-inflation regime rather than a transitory spike.
insights.speaker: James Davolos
insights.so_what: Inflation-linked cash-flow assets are framed as a core allocation rather than a tactical hedge, implying a multi-year holding thesis.
insights.quote: infrastructure oligopolies capable of generating inflation-indexed cash flows

insights.claim: Horizon Kinetics runs the Inflation Beneficiaries ETF (INFL) as its vehicle for this real-assets, royalty, and infrastructure thesis, with Texas Pacific Land (TPL) and MIAX among its concentrated holdings large enough to create affiliate-status trading restrictions.
insights.speaker: Horizon Kinetics
insights.so_what: The firm's outsized, potentially restricted stakes in TPL and MIAX signal high-conviction concentration in scarce-asset royalty and exchange-infrastructure names underlying the broader thesis.
insights.quote: because the Firm has discretion over a substantial percentage of the outstanding shares of TPL and MIAX, it may be deemed to be an affiliate of TPL and MIAX
